Why 2,200

Two plans went into this page. One said 2,300 kcal / 205g protein, the other 2,100 / 210g. Here's the call.

AMaintenance ≈ 2,800

Both plans agree: a 6'0", ~225 lb man who trains burns roughly 2,800 kcal/day.

BThe meals already add to ~2,200

The template day below (460 + 690 + 235 + ~685 + 135) actually totals ≈2,205 kcal and ~210g protein. So 2,200 is what you'll really eat.

C~600 kcal deficit

Fast enough to see weekly progress (~1–1.25 lb/wk), not so aggressive that training and sleep fall apart.

DThen let the scale decide

After 2 weeks: under 0.5 lb/wk → drop to 2,050. Over 1.75 lb/wk or wiped out → go up to 2,350. Protein stays at 205–210g no matter what.

02

The rules that run it

Maintenance is roughly 2,800 kcal a day, so 2,200 puts you in a ~600 kcal deficit. These six rules keep the plan honest without turning it into a second job.

R1Weigh daily, judge weekly

Step on the scale every morning. Only the 7-day average counts — daily numbers are water and noise.

R2Adjust in 150s

After 2 weeks: losing under 0.5 lb/wk → cut 150 kcal. Losing over 1.75 lb/wk → add 150 kcal. Never drop protein. Otherwise hold.

R3Protein anchor

Every meal is built around protein first — ~205–210g/day is what protects muscle while the fat comes off.

R48,000–10,000 steps

Most people sit around 5–6k. Closing that gap is the cheapest fat-loss lever there is — no extra gym time required.

R5Cook twice a week

Sunday + Wednesday, 45–60 minutes each. Everything else is assembly: microwave, air fryer, leftovers.

R6Same skeleton daily

Breakfast, lunch, snack and the evening cup never change. Only dinner rotates — that's what makes it stick.

04b

Sunday prep, minute by minute

About 90 minutes covers Sunday through Wednesday. Wednesday is a 45-minute top-up (rotisserie night + fresh rice + chili into the slow cooker Thursday night).

  1. 0:00Oven to 425°F. Rice cooker on — ~2½ cups dry jasmine (1 : 1.5 water).
  2. 0:05Cube 3 lb potatoes, spray, salt, roast 30 min (flip once).
  3. 0:10Season ~5 lb chicken (garlic, smoked paprika, salt, pepper). Bake 20–22 min to 165°F on the second rack.
  4. 0:15Brown the ground turkey with onion for taco nights. Season, set aside.
  5. 0:40Broccoli into the oven when the potatoes come out (10 min).
  6. 0:55Rest + slice chicken. Portion lunch bowls (180g chicken · 250g rice · 200g broccoli). Fridge 4, freeze the rest.
  7. 1:15Pre-portion yogurt bowls and cottage cheese cups so mornings and nights are grab-and-go. Freeze the second chicken pack for next week.
05

The recipes

Fourteen recipes, best of both plans. Master the batch chicken and the two bowls and you're 80% fed for the week. Costs are per serving at this week's prices.

1 · Greek Yogurt Power Bowl

460 kcal45g protein~$2.05 / serving5 min

Ingredients

  • 340g plain nonfat Greek yogurt
  • 60g rolled oats
  • 100g frozen strawberries
  • Cinnamon + zero-cal sweetener, to taste

Steps

  1. Stir the oats into the yogurt so they soften as it sits.
  2. Fold in the strawberries, cinnamon and sweetener.
  3. Rest 5 minutes — the oats go creamy, the berries thaw just enough. Eat.

2 · Big-Batch Garlic Chicken

Base proteinSunday + Wed25 min

The week's engine — lunch bowls and Tuesday's stir-fry both start here.

Ingredients

  • Chicken breast (~5 lb batch)
  • Garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper

Steps

  1. Season the breasts generously on both sides.
  2. Sheet-pan or air-fryer at 400°F for 20–25 minutes.
  3. Cook to 165°F internal, rest 5 minutes, then slice.
  4. Portion into lunch containers with rice and broccoli.

3 · Chicken Rice Power Bowl

690 kcal67g protein~$1.95 / serving5 min assembly

Ingredients

  • 180g cooked batch chicken
  • 250g cooked jasmine rice
  • 200g frozen broccoli
  • Soy sauce, garlic, hot sauce

Steps

  1. Microwave the broccoli until hot.
  2. Layer rice, chicken and broccoli in a bowl; reheat together.
  3. Finish with soy sauce, garlic and as much hot sauce as you want — those calories are free.

4 · Turkey Taco Plate

685 kcal63g protein~$3.70 · pork swap ~$1.65

Ingredients

  • 93% ground turkey (220g raw weight per plate)
  • Taco seasoning
  • 2 Mission Carb Balance tortillas
  • Salsa, lettuce, 40g reduced-fat cheese

Steps

  1. Brown the turkey in a hot pan, breaking it up fine.
  2. Stir in taco seasoning with a splash of water; simmer 2 minutes.
  3. Load onto warm tortillas with salsa, lettuce and cheese.
The $0.97/lb pork swap

Slice Safeway's pork sirloin chops into thin strips, season exactly like the taco meat and sear hard. Same plate, same macros ballpark — and dinner drops from ~$3.70 to ~$1.65.

5 · Chicken Stir-Fry

~650 kcal60g protein10 min

Ingredients

  • Sliced batch chicken
  • Frozen stir-fry vegetables
  • Soy sauce, garlic, ginger
  • Cooked jasmine rice, to serve

Steps

  1. Sear the frozen veg in a ripping-hot pan until edges char.
  2. Add the sliced chicken just to heat through.
  3. Hit it with soy, garlic and ginger; serve over rice.

6 · Slow-Cooker Turkey Chili

~600 kcal55g protein~$2.40 / servingMakes 4

Ingredients

  • 93% ground turkey
  • Canned kidney beans + black beans, drained
  • Canned tomatoes
  • Onion, chili seasoning

Steps

  1. Brown the turkey and onion; move to the slow cooker.
  2. Add beans, tomatoes and seasoning.
  3. Cook on low 4 hours. Friday dinner + Saturday leftovers, done.

7 · Rotisserie Chicken Plate

~680 kcal60g proteinWednesday

Ingredients

  • Half a Costco rotisserie chicken (the other half is bonus lunch protein)
  • 250g potatoes, air-fried
  • Green beans

Steps

  1. Air-fry cubed potatoes until crisp at the edges.
  2. Steam or microwave the green beans.
  3. Plate a generous portion of chicken with both. Zero real cooking — that's the point of Wednesday.

8 · Egg Scramble

430 kcal42g protein~$1.20 / serving8 min

Ingredients

  • 3 eggs + 200g liquid egg whites (or 5 eggs)
  • Handful of baby spinach
  • Salsa + hot sauce

Steps

  1. Wilt the spinach in the pan first.
  2. Add the eggs and whites; scramble soft.
  3. Top with salsa and hot sauce. Sunday dinner or the breakfast swap.

9 · Sardine Toast

~300 kcal23g protein3 min

Ingredients

  • 1 tin sardines
  • 1 Carb Balance tortilla or light toast
  • Mustard, hot sauce, squeeze of lemon

Steps

  1. Warm the tortilla or toast the bread.
  2. Mash the sardines on top with mustard.
  3. Finish with hot sauce and lemon. Cheap, shelf-stable, loaded with omega-3s.

10 · Cottage Cheese Berry Cup

135 kcal12g protein~$0.85 / serving2 min

Ingredients

  • 100g low-fat cottage cheese
  • 80g frozen blueberries

Steps

  1. Stir the blueberries through the cottage cheese.
  2. That's it — the nightly closer. Slow protein before bed, something sweet that isn't a derailment.

11 · Egg-White Scramble + Berry Oats

490 kcal45g protein8 min

Hot-breakfast alternative to the Power Bowl.

Ingredients

  • 2 whole eggs
  • 1 cup (240g) liquid egg whites
  • ½ cup (40–50g) oats, cooked in water
  • ½ cup berries
  • Salt, pepper, hot sauce, cooking spray

Steps

  1. Microwave the oats in 1 cup water for 2 min; top with berries.
  2. Spray a pan on medium. Whisk eggs into the whites; stir 3–4 min until just set.
  3. Season and eat.

12 · Turkey Taco Skillet + Potatoes

555 kcal45g proteinBatch of 7

A bowl version of taco night — no tortillas, one pan, a week of dinners.

Ingredients

  • ~2.6 lb 93/7 ground turkey (6 oz raw each)
  • 4 cans black beans, rinsed
  • ~3 lb potatoes, cubed
  • 3 bell peppers + 2 onions, diced
  • Taco seasoning + salsa

Steps

  1. Roast the potatoes at 425°F, 30 min, flipping once.
  2. Brown the turkey 8–10 min, breaking it up.
  3. Add peppers + onions 5 min, then seasoning, beans and ½ cup water; simmer 5 min.
  4. Split into 7 containers; salsa on when you reheat.

13 · Protein Yogurt Bowl

290 kcal44g protein2 min

Swap for the shake + banana when you want to chew something.

Ingredients

  • 200g Greek yogurt
  • 1 scoop whey
  • ½ banana, sliced
  • Cinnamon

Steps

  1. Stir the whey into the yogurt (splash of water if thick).
  2. Top with banana and cinnamon.

14 · Zero-Cook Tuna Rice Bowl

~480 kcal~60g protein3 min

For days the chicken runs out.

Ingredients

  • 2 cans tuna (5–7 oz), drained
  • Batch rice + broccoli
  • Lemon, hot sauce

Steps

  1. Swap the tuna in for the lunch-bowl chicken.
  2. Lemon + hot sauce, done.

The supplement stack

Only the basics with real evidence behind them. Everything here is Amazon or Costco, and the whole stack costs less than one tub of the fancy stuff.

Take these

Creatine monohydrate5g/day — BulkSupplements 1 kg, $27.97 on Amazon
$0.14/day
Whey proteinKirkland 5.4 lb, $47.99 at Costco — the daily shake
$0.69/serving
Vitamin D3Daily capsule
~$0.03/day
Fish oilDaily capsule
~$0.20/day
Magnesium glycinateEvening — sleep support
~$0.12/day
Psyllium huskFiber — hunger and fullness on a deficit
~$0.20/day
Caffeine pillsTraining days only
~$0.06
Melatonin (optional)As needed for sleep
~$0.05/day
Whole stack, per month≈ $43–48

Skip these

  • Fat burners — caffeine in a costume, at 10× the price.
  • Testosterone boosters — don't survive the evidence.
  • BCAAs — whey already covers the amino acids.
  • Detox teas — expensive hydration, nothing more.

The deficit does the fat loss. Supplements just cover the gaps — creatine for performance, fiber and protein for hunger, D3 and magnesium because almost everyone runs low.
